data.name: Vergil
data.gender_notes: Vergil is used as a male name in Christian naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Derived from the Latin word ver, meaning 'to tell' or 'to show'. The name Vergil was given to those who acted as messengers or travelers. In Roman mythology, Vergil is the name of a god associated with the Euphrates River. The name Vergil carries the meaning “Traveler, messenger” and is chosen by families in Christian traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Biblical tradition and is also used in English, Greek, Latin. Parents who choose Vergil usually hope their child will grow to embody traveler, messenger and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: A name for those who carry the message of faith.

data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Vergil total 1, giving a life-path number of 1. Number 1 is linked with Sun and with the qualities of leadership, independence and initiative.

data.cultural_impact: Vergil, with its Latin origins, has been deeply rooted in Western culture due to its association with the Roman world. The name has been carried through history by such literary figures as Publius Vergilius Marone (70-19 BC), the greatest of the Roman poets, whose works include The Aeneid – an epic poem that defined and shaped the Roman identity. To this day, Vergil is a name revered within education, language and literature communities.
data.spiritual_significance: From a Christian perspective, Vergil takes on a deeper spiritual significance. The name can be seen as a reminder of God's role as the great "Communicator" and "Traveler" across His universe. Regardless of the meanings attached to the name throughout history, using it as a Christian name reaffirms the belief that our lives are guided by a higher power and that we are all messengers of His Word, conveying and embodying His love in our daily lives.
